summary: Embedding generation seed misalignment during reindexing causing non-deterministic top-K and long-tail rerank latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a recent scheduled reindex, the rerank endpoint returns non-deterministic top-K results for identical queries, and they observe long-tail latency spikes (95th/99th percentile) on rerank calls. This first appeared after a bulk reindex job completed on 2026-03-08.

Impact:
- Affects production search quality for LexSearch customers (some queries return different top results on subsequent identical requests).
- Intermittent latency spikes up to 2–3x baseline on rerank endpoint, causing timeouts in downstream application flow.
- Behavior persists even when requests are pinned to the same model and replica.

Environment / Context:
- Customer uses Dedicated capacity in us-east-1 with pinned embedding model embed-large-v2 and rerank model rerank-small-v1.
- Bulk reindex job executed against their namespace (ns: lex-articles) using our indexer service; reindex used the offline batch-worker fleet with version tag indexer-2026-03-07.
- Embeddings were generated as part of the reindex; embedding payloads show expected dimension (1536) and types (float32), but similarity scores vary between requests.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Send identical search query payloads (same prompt, same rerank params) to rerank endpoint 3x spaced 10s apart.
2) Observe top-K list differs between calls ~30% of the time for certain queries.
3) Observe 95th/99th percentile latency increase correlated with mismatched top-K sets.

Observed logs/snippets (customer provided):
- Rerank request IDs: rr-20260308-abc123, rr-20260308-def456
- Timestamps show occasional GPU fallback to CPU path (serving-runtime: fallback=cpu, reason=\"kv-cache-miss-random\")
- Indexer logs during reindex: \"seed: unset; using system RNG\" and later \"completed batch 42/421\"

Customer workaround in place:
- Customer rolled back to previous index snapshot (pre-reindex) which removed nondeterminism for several hours. When re-running the reindex with the same job parameters, issue reappears randomly.

Desired outcome:
- Deterministic rerank results for identical inputs when underlying index and models are unchanged.
- Eliminate long-tail latency spikes and reduce CPU fallbacks tied to this issue.
comments: 2026-03-09 - Nina Patel (Support): Logged initial ticket after verifying reindex job timestamp and customer-provided logs. Requested full indexer job manifest and sample request/response pairs.

2026-03-09 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Noted that indexer batches historically used a deterministic seed when --seed is provided; manifest shows --seed omitted. Asked engineering to confirm default behavior of offline batch-worker RNG across fleet restarts.

2026-03-10 - Customer (LexSearch Technical Lead): Provided reindex job manifest and two sample request IDs. Confirmed that reindex was started at 2026-03-08T03:12:00Z and completed at 2026-03-08T07:45:00Z.

2026-03-10 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Reproduced nondeterministic top-K locally by running subset of indexer with RNG unset. Observed embedding micro-variance leading to stable top-K flips for items near decision boundary. Filed engineering hypothesis for seed and normalization differences.

2026-03-11 - Alice Wong (Applied ML): Confirmed that embed-large-v2 uses stochastic dropout-like ops when run in training mode; offline indexer must enforce eval mode and a deterministic RNG seed to get bit-identical embeddings. Noted two indexer images used during the job: indexer-2026-03-07 (eval mode) and indexer-2026-03-07+hotfix (forgot eval flag).
2026-03-11 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Instrumented reindexer to record --seed and model-mode flags on every batch. Scheduled a controlled reindex with explicit seed and model static-mode to validate fix.
2026-03-11 - Customer: Requested ETA for permanent remediation and confirmation that future reindexes will not introduce nondeterminism.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Indexer run omitted deterministic seed and inadvertently used a model image that executed stochastic ops (training-mode or non-deterministic kernels), producing micro-variance across embeddings leading to different top-K ordering for borderline candidates.
Hypothesis 2: KV cache keying uses a checksum of embedding bytes; small embedding variance causes cache misses triggering CPU fallback path for certain rerank requests, adding long-tail latency.

Evidence: Local reproduction showed top-K flips when reindex run omitted --seed and when model checkpoint was instantiated without eval flag. Profiling of rerank path shows increased CPU fallback rate correlated with cache-miss logs.
Telemetry: Increased 95th/99th latency for rerank endpoint correlated to reindex completion window in customer namespace. No global region-wide spike observed.
Action: Added temporary guarding to indexer orchestration to require explicit --seed and --model-mode=eval; added logging of seed and model flags to job metadata.
resolution_notes: Root cause: Offline reindex job ran multiple batch-worker variants; one variant invoked the embedding model in a non-deterministic mode (training-like ops) and indexer orchestration omitted a fixed RNG seed. This produced micro-variance in embeddings resulting in non-deterministic top-K and invalidating prefix/KV cache hits that triggered CPU fallbacks and long-tail latency.

Fixes applied:
- Immediate: Rolled forward an indexer hotfix that enforces --seed=<job-uuid-derived> and --model-mode=eval for all offline batch-worker runs. Re-ran the customer's reindex under controlled conditions and confirmed deterministic top-K across repeated identical queries. Restored normal latency percentiles.
- Medium-term: Added a deployment check to the indexer pipeline that fails runs if model image does not assert eval-mode at startup. Added an indexer job metadata field 'embedding-seed' that is stored with index snapshot for auditability.
- Long-term: Engineering to add CI test that samples identical input through the full offline reindex path and asserts embedding checksum stability when seed and eval-mode are set.
Rollout notes: Hotfix rolled to dedicated fleet in us-east-1 only; scheduled global rollout next week. Notified affected customer and provided reindex support window to remediate impacted namespaces.
Follow-ups: Create runbook step in 'Embed-Reindexing-Runbook' about mandatory seed and model-mode flags; update customer-facing docs for reindex best practices.
resolution: In Progress - hotfix deployed to customer fleet and controlled reindex validated. Global rollout and CI tests scheduled. Customer notified and offered assisted reindex; pending confirmation from engineering on global rollout window.
